profiles.name: Katelyn Skye Seitz
profiles.description: Katelyn Skye Seitz, who publicly identifies themself as Skye Jones, was arrested during a January 9, 2026 demonstration outside the federal immigration building in Santa Ana, California. The protest followed the killing of Renee Good by a federal immigration agent in Minneapolis. A federal complaint accused Seitz of throwing an orange traffic cone, resisting arrest, and striking an officer. Seitz spent the weekend in Santa Ana City Jail and was released after an initial hearing on January 12.
profiles.finding: Santa Ana court calendar and case coverage corroborate identity. Obituary same full name does not establish portrait; no verified image located.

profiles.name: Wil Casey Floyd
profiles.description: Wil Casey Floyd, age 33, of Elkhart Lake WI, was sentenced to 37 months federal prison for unlawful possession of a destructive device; he made and threw Molotov cocktails at police officers during the May 1, 2016 Black Bloc May Day parade in Seattle, igniting one officers trousers and burning his legs.
profiles.finding: Seattle Weekly and SeattlePI case reporting identifies protest imagery; no usable individual portrait verified.
profiles.query: "Wil Casey Floyd" Seattle May Day photo

profiles.name: Sam Jessup
profiles.description: Samuel L. “Sam” Jessup was the videographer for the October 11, 2016 Climate Direct Action pipeline shutdown in North Dakota. He livestreamed Michael Foster’s closure of a TransCanada Keystone pipeline valve and was arrested with Foster. A jury convicted Jessup in October 2017 of conspiracy to commit criminal mischief and conspiracy to commit criminal trespass. On February 6, 2018, the court deferred a two-year prison term and placed him on supervised probation for two years; he did not receive an executed jail or prison sentence.
profiles.finding: High Plains Reader and Seattle Met corroborate valve-turner support role; marketing MBA namesake not linked; no portrait verified.

profiles.name: Justin Gray Liverman
profiles.description: Justin Gray Liverman, known online as D3F4ULT, participated in Crackas With Attitude, a politically motivated hacking collective. He pleaded guilty to a conspiracy involving computer intrusions, identity theft and telephone harassment and served federal prison time.
profiles.finding: Ars/VICE and DOJ plea corroborate hacker identity; generic hacker illustrations excluded; no verified portrait.

profiles.name: Mr. Kim Guk-Nam
profiles.description:
Mr. Kim Guk-Nam is a Korean Jeju Naval Base resister. Refusal to pay fines for resistance to naval base construction.

Since 2007, the South Korean government has been constructing a major naval base on Gangjeong village, Jeju Island — a UNESCO biosphere reserve and South Korea's southernmost island. The base, designed to host U.S. and South Korean Aegis destroyers and a port-of-call for U.S. nuclear-powered aircraft carriers, is widely understood as a forward-deployment site for the U.S. military's posture against China. Local Gangjeong residents and Korean peace activists have maintained continuous nonviolent resistance at the construction gates since 2010; hundreds have been arrested and dozens have served Korean prison sentences for trespass, obstruction, and civil disobedience.
profiles.finding: Nuclear Resister indexed caption explicitly credits Yoonmadam; original monthly archive now404 and web fetch fails. NR180 PDF remains recovery lead.

profiles.name: Michael Skidmore
profiles.description: Michael Skidmore was a 58-year-old retired state corrections officer and public-records activist in Mansfield, Ohio. He regularly requested public documents and attended Richland County commissioners' meetings. On July 9, 2015, while he was recording a public meeting with a camera attached to a lanyard around his neck, courthouse security tried to take the camera and an altercation followed; a security officer's gun discharged into a wall. A jury acquitted Skidmore of two felonious-assault counts but convicted him of two assault counts, inducing panic, and obstructing official business. On July 27, 2016, he was sentenced to an aggregate 16 months of incarceration. The Ohio Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment in 2017.
profiles.finding: Mansfield query returns numerous unrelated actor, NYC civic, fishing, Japan-history and Florida booking identities; none linked. News Journal original remains lead.

profiles.name: Timothy Justen French
profiles.description: Timothy Justen French, known online as Orbit and by several related aliases, participated in the hacking groups NullCrew and Anonymous. Federal prosecutors said he took part in at least seven attacks on companies, universities, and government entities between 2012 and 2014. French pleaded guilty in December 2015 to intentionally damaging a protected computer without authorization. He received a 45-month federal sentence on November 1, 2016. After a period in a halfway house and a later return to custody, a prisoner-support project reported his final release on January 14, 2019.
profiles.finding: Myspace exact full name and Morristown location promising but not independently tied to case. CyberCrime blog images mostly contextual; DOJ case corroborates, no accepted portrait.

profiles.name: Jedidiah Poole
profiles.description:
Jedidiah Poole — SOA Watch line-crosser at Fort Benning, Georgia. Convicted of trespass on a military installation and sentenced to 3 months in federal custody.

Each November on the anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: Exact name and SOA Watch searches lack a verified result; similarly spelled Jedidah Poole excluded.

profiles.finding: FBI case and Cryptosphere support list corroborate identity; no accepted portrait; commenter avatars excluded.

profiles.name: Liam Mulholland
profiles.description: Liam Mulholland, age 18 at indictment, pleaded guilty in 2013 to 18 USC 844(i) arson involving interstate commerce for a 2003 ELF-claimed firebombing of a Mystic Forest housing-development home in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Cooperated with the FBI; received 18 months federal prison.

profiles.name: Julio Zuniga
profiles.description: Julio A. "Comrade Z" Zuniga, from San Antonio, is an anarchist prisoner-organizer in the Texas prison system, an Incarcerated Workers Organizing Committee member who has organized work stoppages against unpaid prison labor, written widely from inside, and spent long stretches in solitary confinement in retaliation — much of his 2018-2023 time at the Darrington/Memorial Unit was spent in isolation before a transfer to the Ramsey Unit. In April 2024 the parole board denied his release, setting him back roughly four and a half more years.
profiles.finding: Libcom and Prison Phone Justice identify Comrade Z; no usable verified portrait extracted. Athlete, obituary and Honduran namesakes excluded.

profiles.name: Emily Gillespie
profiles.description: Emily “Gabby” Gillespie is an environmental activist from Roanoke, Virginia, whose work with Mountain Justice drew on Appalachian women’s history of nonviolent resistance. She joined the May 24, 2013 blockade of the access road to Alpha Natural Resources headquarters in Bristol, Virginia. On July 25, she pleaded guilty to blocking a public roadway, received a 90-day sentence with 80 days suspended, and entered the Bristol jail. She was released for good behavior on July 29 after five days.
profiles.finding: Earth First and Mountain Justice sentencing reporting identify activist; Toronto author, journalist and travel influencer unlinked; reject.

profiles.description: Justin Raymond Colby was a U.S. servicemember who refused deployment during the Iraq/Afghanistan wars. Military refuser, SOA Watch protester. Sentenced to 9 months.
profiles.finding: Nuclear Resister171 identifies soldier sentence; no verified portrait located.

profiles.name: Kevin Chianella
profiles.description: Kevin Chianella is a U.S. anarchist who participated in the June 26, 2010 protests against the G20 summit in Toronto. Canadian authorities accused him of offenses connected with property damage and confrontations during the demonstrations. Chianella surrendered to U.S. marshals on February 28, 2013, waived extradition, and was transferred to Canadian custody on March 5. After release on bail, he pleaded guilty on February 13, 2014 to 16 of the original 53 counts and received a 24-month federal penitentiary sentence. Contemporary prisoner-support reports placed him first at Joyceville Institution and later at Beaver Creek Institution.
profiles.finding: NYCABC/GuelphABC case corroboration and organizer's GoFundMe portrait lead; identity connection requires verification before use.

Piratheepan Nadarajah conspired with an undercover FBI agent to purchase $1 million worth of weapons for the Tamil Tigers.
